question_text: Which frequency band is most commonly used for mobile satellite phone handsets because it penetrates foliage well and suffers relatively little atmospheric attenuation?
options: Ka-band (26.5–40 GHz)
V-band (40–75 GHz)
mmWave FR2 (24–52 GHz)
L-band (approximately 1–2 GHz)
correct_answer: L-band (approximately 1–2 GHz)

question_text: NTN is particularly well-suited for narrowband IoT (NB-IoT) deployments primarily because:
options: IoT devices require very high bandwidth that only satellites can provide
NTN never supports IoT, which is a terrestrial-only service
IoT devices are often in remote areas without terrestrial coverage, and their low data-rate requirements are compatible with satellite link constraints
IoT battery life is too short for any terrestrial network
correct_answer: IoT devices are often in remote areas without terrestrial coverage, and their low data-rate requirements are compatible with satellite link constraints

question_text: The Starlink constellation by SpaceX provides broadband primarily from which orbital shell?
options: GEO at 35,786 km, using three satellites
MEO at 20,200 km, like GPS
LEO at around 550 km, using thousands of satellites for global coverage
HAPS at 20 km altitude
correct_answer: LEO at around 550 km, using thousands of satellites for global coverage

question_text: The Iridium system is notable for using inter-satellite links (ISLs) and for being able to route calls between satellites without a ground gateway underneath every satellite. Its constellation consists of:
options: 3 GEO satellites covering only the tropics
24 MEO satellites identical to the GPS constellation
Thousands of HAPS platforms in the stratosphere
66 LEO satellites providing polar and global coverage
correct_answer: 66 LEO satellites providing polar and global coverage

question_text: 3GPP Release 17 is significant to NTN because it:
options: Defined the basic 5G NR air interface with no NTN provisions
Introduced the first standardised 5G NR enhancements specifically for satellite access, including timing and Doppler adaptations
Removed NTN support that had been added in Release 15
Only addressed mmWave terrestrial enhancements
correct_answer: Introduced the first standardised 5G NR enhancements specifically for satellite access, including timing and Doppler adaptations

question_text: Direct-to-Device (D2X) satellite services, which allow an unmodified smartphone to communicate via satellite, are enabled primarily by:
options: A dedicated satellite handset sold only by satellite operators
Special IoT modules embedded at the factory that are not part of 3GPP
New 3GPP NTN specifications that extend 5G NR for low-power handheld UEs accessing satellites directly
A terrestrial base station located near the satellite ground track
correct_answer: New 3GPP NTN specifications that extend 5G NR for low-power handheld UEs accessing satellites directly

question_text: A key advantage of NTN as a complement to terrestrial networks is that during large public events or disasters, NTN can:
options: Replace the terrestrial network permanently after the event
Offload or supplement congested terrestrial cells, providing capacity relief and backup connectivity
Provide lower latency than any terrestrial alternative
Prevent any interference to the terrestrial network
correct_answer: Offload or supplement congested terrestrial cells, providing capacity relief and backup connectivity

question_text: As satellite altitude increases, the coverage footprint of a single satellite:
options: Increases, but at the cost of longer propagation delay and higher free-space path loss
Decreases, because higher satellites transmit at lower power
Remains constant regardless of altitude
Increases, with no effect on propagation delay
correct_answer: Increases, but at the cost of longer propagation delay and higher free-space path loss

question_text: In the 6G vision, NTN is regarded as:
options: A temporary solution to be replaced by dense urban 6G cells
Exclusively a backhaul technology, not a direct user-access layer
A 4G-only technology being phased out for 5G
A native component providing the 'coverage everywhere' pillar alongside terrestrial networks
correct_answer: A native component providing the 'coverage everywhere' pillar alongside terrestrial networks

question_text: In a LEO NTN system, a UE may experience two types of handover: satellite-to-satellite (inter-satellite) and beam-to-beam within the same satellite (inter-beam). Both require:
options: No signalling, because the satellite tracks the UE autonomously
Mobility management procedures adapted to the rapidly changing satellite geometry
Only GEO-specific procedures, as LEO uses a different standard
Physical reconnection of the UE to a different ground gateway
correct_answer: Mobility management procedures adapted to the rapidly changing satellite geometry

question_text: Compared with GEO, LEO satellites offer lower latency because:
options: LEO satellites transmit at higher power than GEO
LEO satellites use a higher carrier frequency than GEO
Their altitude is roughly 550–1,500 km vs 35,786 km for GEO, greatly reducing one-way propagation delay
LEO satellites are physically smaller and therefore faster
correct_answer: Their altitude is roughly 550–1,500 km vs 35,786 km for GEO, greatly reducing one-way propagation delay

question_text: Satellite link power limitation arises primarily because:
options: Spectrum regulations prohibit satellites from transmitting above a certain power
The ground terminal regulates the satellite's power remotely
The satellite's transmit power is constrained by the solar panel area and mass budget available in orbit
Higher power always degrades signal quality in satellite systems
correct_answer: The satellite's transmit power is constrained by the solar panel area and mass budget available in orbit

question_text: The large round-trip time of a GEO satellite link causes problems for the TCP protocol because:
options: TCP ignores propagation delay entirely and is unaffected
Large RTT increases the TCP window size automatically, improving throughput
The TCP congestion window fills slowly, capping throughput unless a Performance-Enhancing Proxy (PEP) or TCP optimisation is used
TCP was designed for satellite links and performs better over GEO than over terrestrial
correct_answer: The TCP congestion window fills slowly, capping throughput unless a Performance-Enhancing Proxy (PEP) or TCP optimisation is used

question_text: Spot beams in a satellite system concentrate transmit power onto a smaller geographic area in order to:
options: Reduce the satellite's power consumption
Increase the power spectral density within each beam and enable frequency reuse across spatially separated beams
Illuminate the entire Earth from a single antenna element
Eliminate the need for frequency planning between beams
correct_answer: Increase the power spectral density within each beam and enable frequency reuse across spatially separated beams

question_text: 3GPP defines two categories of NTN UE based on their ability to assist Doppler and timing compensation. These are:
options: Voice-only UEs and data-only UEs
GNSS-capable UEs (which pre-compensate using their own position and ephemeris) and non-GNSS UEs (which rely on network assistance)
Fixed UEs and mobile UEs
Transparent UEs and regenerative UEs
correct_answer: GNSS-capable UEs (which pre-compensate using their own position and ephemeris) and non-GNSS UEs (which rely on network assistance)

question_text: Satellite spectrum coordination at the international level is managed primarily through:
options: WTO BTA tariff schedules
UN Security Council resolutions
The 3GPP technical specification process
ITU Radio Regulations, bilateral and multilateral agreements between administrations
correct_answer: ITU Radio Regulations, bilateral and multilateral agreements between administrations

question_text: In a bent-pipe (transparent) transponder, noise accumulated on the uplink is:
options: Amplified and retransmitted alongside the signal, degrading the overall downlink carrier-to-noise ratio
Completely removed by the low-noise amplifier before retransmission
Only present on the downlink, not the uplink
Eliminated by the frequency-conversion process
correct_answer: Amplified and retransmitted alongside the signal, degrading the overall downlink carrier-to-noise ratio

question_text: Ephemeris data used by NTN UEs describes:
options: The satellite's onboard power budget
The list of licensed operators permitted to use the satellite
The predicted position and velocity of the satellite over time, enabling the UE to compute Doppler shift and propagation delay
The software version running on the satellite payload
correct_answer: The predicted position and velocity of the satellite over time, enabling the UE to compute Doppler shift and propagation delay

question_text: GNSS assists NTN UEs primarily by providing:
options: A replacement for the NTN service link in areas of poor satellite visibility
Accurate UE position, which combined with satellite ephemeris allows the UE to pre-compensate Doppler shift and timing advance
Electrical power to the UE's radio module
Direct connection to the 5G core network via GNSS satellites
correct_answer: Accurate UE position, which combined with satellite ephemeris allows the UE to pre-compensate Doppler shift and timing advance

question_text: Maritime vessels in open ocean beyond terrestrial coastal coverage rely on NTN for:
options: Broadband internet, voice, safety and vessel-tracking services
VHF terrestrial radio connections to land-based towers
Fibre undersea cable connections carried by the vessel
Microwave line-of-sight links between ships
correct_answer: Broadband internet, voice, safety and vessel-tracking services

question_text: In-flight connectivity (IFC) for commercial aircraft is provided by NTN because:
options: Aviation regulations require aircraft to use terrestrial cellular only
Aircraft at cruise altitude are beyond the range of terrestrial networks, requiring satellite links for passenger and cockpit communications
Aircraft antennas are incompatible with satellite frequencies
In-flight connectivity is delivered by HF radio, not satellites
correct_answer: Aircraft at cruise altitude are beyond the range of terrestrial networks, requiring satellite links for passenger and cockpit communications

question_text: Circular polarization is preferred over linear polarization for mobile satellite terminals because:
options: Circular polarization suffers less rain attenuation than linear polarization
The received signal polarization is independent of the terminal's physical orientation, simplifying the antenna design
Linear polarization cannot be received by any satellite antenna
Circular polarization always achieves higher gain than linear polarization
correct_answer: The received signal polarization is independent of the terminal's physical orientation, simplifying the antenna design

question_text: The OneWeb LEO constellation differs from Starlink in that OneWeb focuses on:
options: Launching GEO satellites for direct-to-consumer TV broadcasting
Operating exclusively in Ka-band for military applications
Using only bent-pipe payloads with no IP routing onboard
Providing broadband connectivity through a wholesale/B2B model, selling capacity to telecom operators rather than directly to consumers
correct_answer: Providing broadband connectivity through a wholesale/B2B model, selling capacity to telecom operators rather than directly to consumers

question_text: A Performance-Enhancing Proxy (PEP) on a satellite gateway improves TCP throughput by:
options: Increasing the satellite's transmit power automatically
Replacing TCP with a proprietary transport protocol at the UE
Splitting the TCP connection into a terrestrial segment and a satellite segment, hiding the large satellite RTT from the end-to-end TCP feedback loop
Reducing the number of TCP acknowledgements the server must send
correct_answer: Splitting the TCP connection into a terrestrial segment and a satellite segment, hiding the large satellite RTT from the end-to-end TCP feedback loop

question_text: Which NTN platform offers the most rapid deployment and easiest recovery after failure, but is most limited by weather and flight regulations?
options: GEO satellite, which can be repositioned within hours
LEO satellite, which can be lowered to 50 km on demand
Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS/drone) used as an airborne NTN node
HAPS balloon, which is immune to strong winds
correct_answer: Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS/drone) used as an airborne NTN node

question_text: Free-space path loss (FSPL) increases with distance and frequency according to FSPL(dB) = 20 log(d) + 20 log(f) + constant. A doubling of the carrier frequency therefore increases FSPL by approximately:
options: 3 dB
10 dB
6 dB
0 dB — frequency has no effect on free-space path loss
correct_answer: 6 dB

question_text: Rain attenuation is most severe at which frequency range?
options: Below 2 GHz (L-band), where wavelengths are long relative to raindrop size
At optical wavelengths only, not at microwave frequencies
Above approximately 10 GHz (Ku, Ka and higher bands), where raindrops are comparable in size to the signal wavelength
Between 400 and 700 MHz (UHF), where absorption is strongest
correct_answer: Above approximately 10 GHz (Ku, Ka and higher bands), where raindrops are comparable in size to the signal wavelength

question_text: A satellite orbit's inclination is defined as:
options: The altitude of the satellite above sea level
The angle between the orbital plane and the Earth's equatorial plane; 0° is equatorial (GEO), 90° is polar
The eccentricity of the orbital ellipse
The angle between the satellite's antenna and the Earth's surface
correct_answer: The angle between the orbital plane and the Earth's equatorial plane; 0° is equatorial (GEO), 90° is polar

question_text: A sun-synchronous orbit is used by Earth-observation satellites because:
options: The satellite orbits the Sun rather than the Earth, providing global energy coverage
The satellite is stationary above the same point on Earth at all times
Solar panels on a sun-synchronous satellite are always perpendicular to the Sun
The orbital plane precesses at the same rate as the Earth's revolution around the Sun, keeping the local solar illumination time constant over each pass
correct_answer: The orbital plane precesses at the same rate as the Earth's revolution around the Sun, keeping the local solar illumination time constant over each pass

question_text: The Van Allen radiation belts are a concern for satellite designers because:
options: They are zones of trapped high-energy charged particles that can degrade semiconductor electronics and solar cells
They cause rain attenuation on Ku-band downlinks
They prevent radio signals from reaching GEO altitude
They are cloud layers in the troposphere that scatter microwave signals
correct_answer: They are zones of trapped high-energy charged particles that can degrade semiconductor electronics and solar cells

question_text: The ionosphere (roughly 60–1,000 km altitude) affects satellite radio signals primarily by causing:
options: Rain fade and tropospheric scintillation above 10 GHz
Inter-symbol interference caused by multipath from buildings
Propagation delay, Faraday rotation of polarization, and signal dispersion, particularly at frequencies below about 3 GHz
Thermal noise amplification in the satellite LNA
correct_answer: Propagation delay, Faraday rotation of polarization, and signal dispersion, particularly at frequencies below about 3 GHz

question_text: Tropospheric scintillation is a rapid fluctuation of received signal amplitude and phase caused by turbulence in the lower atmosphere. It is most significant at:
options: High elevation angles and low frequencies below 1 GHz
All elevation angles equally, independent of frequency
Low elevation angles and frequencies above about 10 GHz
Polar latitudes only, where the troposphere is thinner
correct_answer: Low elevation angles and frequencies above about 10 GHz

question_text: The Doppler frequency shift experienced by a ground receiver tracking a LEO satellite depends primarily on:
options: The radial component of the satellite's velocity relative to the receiver, and the carrier frequency
Only the satellite's altitude, not its velocity
Only the carrier frequency, not the satellite's motion
The polarization of the signal, not the satellite geometry
correct_answer: The radial component of the satellite's velocity relative to the receiver, and the carrier frequency

question_text: A GEO satellite produces negligible Doppler shift for a stationary ground terminal because:
options: GEO satellites orbit too slowly to produce any relative motion
Both the satellite and the terminal are effectively stationary relative to each other — the satellite's angular velocity matches the Earth's rotation
Doppler shift is cancelled by the transponder's frequency converter
GEO satellites transmit a compensation tone that removes Doppler
correct_answer: Both the satellite and the terminal are effectively stationary relative to each other — the satellite's angular velocity matches the Earth's rotation

question_text: The elevation angle of a satellite as seen from a ground station determines:
options: The satellite's orbital altitude above sea level
The satellite's velocity relative to the ground
The number of other satellites visible from the ground station
The length of the signal path through the atmosphere; higher elevation means a shorter atmospheric path and less attenuation
correct_answer: The length of the signal path through the atmosphere; higher elevation means a shorter atmospheric path and less attenuation

question_text: Link margin in a satellite system is defined as:
options: The physical diameter of the satellite's main reflector antenna
The maximum allowable data rate on the satellite link
The ratio of transmit power to receive power at the ground station
The excess of received Eb/N0 (or C/N0) above the minimum threshold required for the specified bit-error rate
correct_answer: The excess of received Eb/N0 (or C/N0) above the minimum threshold required for the specified bit-error rate

question_text: During equinox periods, GEO satellites experience solar eclipses lasting up to about:
options: 72 minutes per day, during which the satellite relies on onboard batteries
12 hours per day, as the satellite is behind the Earth all night
Under 1 minute, since the Earth's shadow is very narrow at GEO
GEO satellites never experience eclipse because they orbit the equatorial plane
correct_answer: 72 minutes per day, during which the satellite relies on onboard batteries

question_text: Frequency reuse in a multi-beam satellite system increases overall system capacity because:
options: Each beam uses a different frequency, and reuse simply means the spectrum plan repeats
Frequency reuse reduces co-channel interference to zero
The same frequency band is reused across spatially separated beams, multiplying the total traffic the satellite can carry
Total system capacity is limited by the number of beams regardless of reuse
correct_answer: The same frequency band is reused across spatially separated beams, multiplying the total traffic the satellite can carry

question_text: When the same frequency is used in adjacent satellite beams (co-channel reuse), co-channel interference (CCI) is controlled by:
options: Sufficient beam spacing and antenna sidelobe suppression to keep the interfering signal below acceptable levels
Increasing the carrier frequency until adjacent beams no longer overlap
Assigning different polarizations to every beam
Requiring adjacent beams to transmit at exactly the same power level
correct_answer: Sufficient beam spacing and antenna sidelobe suppression to keep the interfering signal below acceptable levels

question_text: By Kepler's third law, the orbital period of a satellite is proportional to the cube root of the cube of the semi-major axis (T² ∝ a³). This means:
options: Higher orbits have shorter periods and higher orbital speeds
The orbital period is the same regardless of altitude
Higher orbits have longer periods and lower orbital speeds than lower orbits
The orbital period depends on satellite mass, not altitude
correct_answer: Higher orbits have longer periods and lower orbital speeds than lower orbits

question_text: GEO satellites have poor coverage poleward of approximately ±75° latitude because:
options: The Van Allen belts block radio signals at polar latitudes
International regulations prohibit GEO satellite transmissions above 75° latitude
They orbit in the equatorial plane, so the elevation angle seen from high latitudes is very low, below the horizon or near it
Ionospheric absorption is so high at the poles that any signal is lost
correct_answer: They orbit in the equatorial plane, so the elevation angle seen from high latitudes is very low, below the horizon or near it

question_text: A Molniya orbit is a highly elliptical orbit (HEO) with an inclination of about 63.4° and a 12-hour period. Its primary purpose is to:
options: Provide geostationary-like fixed coverage over the equator
Achieve the lowest possible propagation delay for Arctic users
Provide long-dwell coverage of high-latitude regions (such as Russia) where GEO elevation angles are too low
Allow satellites to pass over the equator at least four times per day
correct_answer: Provide long-dwell coverage of high-latitude regions (such as Russia) where GEO elevation angles are too low

question_text: The Iridium constellation routes calls via inter-satellite links (ISLs), which means:
options: Calls between any two points on Earth can be routed entirely through the satellite network without requiring a ground gateway in between
Each call must pass through a dedicated gateway for every hop
ISLs are used only for housekeeping telemetry, not user traffic
Iridium ISLs operate in the optical band and cannot carry voice
correct_answer: Calls between any two points on Earth can be routed entirely through the satellite network without requiring a ground gateway in between

question_text: The ITU-R rain zone classification system (zones A to Q) is used to:
options: Regulate the maximum allowable satellite transmit power in each zone
Classify the orbital slots available to geostationary satellites
Define the spectrum allocations for different satellite services
Estimate the rain attenuation statistics for a given geographic location and design satellite link margins accordingly
correct_answer: Estimate the rain attenuation statistics for a given geographic location and design satellite link margins accordingly

question_text: A multi-beam satellite antenna produces higher gain per beam than a global beam antenna. The trade-off is that:
options: Each beam consumes more power, reducing total satellite capacity
Multi-beam antennas cannot reuse frequencies between beams
Higher gain per beam means lower overall system throughput
Each beam covers a smaller geographic area, requiring more beams to achieve the same total coverage
correct_answer: Each beam covers a smaller geographic area, requiring more beams to achieve the same total coverage

question_text: The geosynchronous orbit is the set of all orbits with a 24-hour period, while the geostationary orbit (GEO) is a subset defined by:
options: Zero inclination (equatorial plane) and zero eccentricity (circular orbit), resulting in a fixed position above the equator
A highly elliptical orbit with an inclination of 63.4°
Any polar orbit with a 24-hour period
An inclination of exactly 28.5°, the latitude of the main launch sites
correct_answer: Zero inclination (equatorial plane) and zero eccentricity (circular orbit), resulting in a fixed position above the equator

question_text: Satellite eclipse occurs when the Earth's shadow blocks sunlight from reaching the satellite. During eclipse, the satellite continues operating because:
options: Solar panels store energy chemically without needing batteries
A backup nuclear power unit activates during eclipse
The satellite automatically reduces power to zero and waits for sunlight
Onboard batteries are charged during sunlit periods and supply power during eclipse
correct_answer: Onboard batteries are charged during sunlit periods and supply power during eclipse

question_text: The figure of merit G/T of a satellite receiver system improves (increases) when:
options: Antenna receive gain G increases or system noise temperature T decreases
Path loss increases
The transmitter EIRP decreases
The carrier frequency decreases while G and T remain constant
correct_answer: Antenna receive gain G increases or system noise temperature T decreases

question_text: In the link budget of a satellite system, the overall end-to-end performance is determined by:
options: The sum of the uplink and downlink C/N values in linear scale
The uplink only, since the satellite amplifies the downlink without adding noise
The weaker of the uplink and downlink, since the total signal-to-noise ratio is dominated by the noisier hop
The downlink only, since the uplink is always in surplus
correct_answer: The weaker of the uplink and downlink, since the total signal-to-noise ratio is dominated by the noisier hop

question_text: Polarization diversity allows a satellite to reuse the same frequency band twice by transmitting two independent signals using:
options: Two different carrier frequencies in the same polarization
Orthogonal polarizations (e.g., horizontal and vertical linear, or RHCP and LHCP circular)
Two identical signals with a phase offset of 90 degrees
Two antennas pointing at different geographic areas
correct_answer: Orthogonal polarizations (e.g., horizontal and vertical linear, or RHCP and LHCP circular)

question_text: 3GPP Release 17 introduced the first NTN-specific 5G NR enhancements, which included adaptations to timing advance, Doppler compensation and:
options: Removal of the OFDM waveform in favour of a satellite-specific scheme
A dedicated NTN frequency band below 100 MHz
Replacement of the 5G core network with a satellite-specific core
HARQ process design to handle the long satellite round-trip time
correct_answer: HARQ process design to handle the long satellite round-trip time

question_text: In NTN, an extended Timing Advance (TA) mechanism is required because:
options: The satellite's clock runs faster than the ground station's clock
Timing advance is used to delay the downlink signal to match user location
Propagation delays of tens to hundreds of milliseconds must be pre-compensated so that uplink transmissions arrive at the gNB within the correct slot boundary
TA is needed only when the UE is stationary; it is disabled for moving UEs
correct_answer: Propagation delays of tens to hundreds of milliseconds must be pre-compensated so that uplink transmissions arrive at the gNB within the correct slot boundary

question_text: The PRACH (Physical Random Access Channel) preamble design is modified for NTN by:
options: Extending the preamble length and guard period to accommodate the large round-trip propagation delay, preventing preamble collisions
Shortening preambles to reduce overhead in the long-delay channel
Using a CDMA spreading code instead of a Zadoff-Chu sequence
Transmitting the PRACH on the downlink rather than the uplink
correct_answer: Extending the preamble length and guard period to accommodate the large round-trip propagation delay, preventing preamble collisions

question_text: The fundamental problem HARQ faces in a GEO NTN system is that:
options: HARQ acknowledgements are encrypted, causing decoding delays
HARQ retransmissions travel faster than the original transmission
The RTT in GEO is the same as in terrestrial NR, so HARQ is unaffected
The 500+ ms RTT means the transmitter must buffer many HARQ processes simultaneously, far exceeding the 8-ms terrestrial HARQ round-trip budget
correct_answer: The 500+ ms RTT means the transmitter must buffer many HARQ processes simultaneously, far exceeding the 8-ms terrestrial HARQ round-trip budget

question_text: For GEO NTN, 3GPP permits HARQ to be disabled. When HARQ feedback is turned off, residual errors are handled by:
options: The satellite's onboard processor, which corrects errors in orbit
Outer-layer error recovery mechanisms such as RLC ARQ or application-layer FEC
Increasing UE transmit power until no errors occur
Repeating every transmission exactly twice regardless of error status
correct_answer: Outer-layer error recovery mechanisms such as RLC ARQ or application-layer FEC

question_text: As a LEO satellite moves, beam management in NTN must handle:
options: Static beam assignments that never change during a session
Only uplink beam management, since the downlink is always optimal
Beam management identical to that used in terrestrial massive MIMO
Beam sweeping, beam measurement reporting, and beam failure recovery adapted to the satellite's high angular velocity relative to the ground
correct_answer: Beam sweeping, beam measurement reporting, and beam failure recovery adapted to the satellite's high angular velocity relative to the ground

question_text: In a LEO NTN with Earth-moving beams, the cell associated with a given geographic area changes as the satellite passes overhead. 3GPP addresses this by:
options: Distinguishing between Earth-fixed and Earth-moving cell identities, and adapting cell re-selection and handover procedures accordingly
Assigning a permanent cell ID to each geographic point on Earth, independent of the satellite
Requiring UEs to switch to a terrestrial network during the cell transition
Eliminating the cell concept entirely in NTN
correct_answer: Distinguishing between Earth-fixed and Earth-moving cell identities, and adapting cell re-selection and handover procedures accordingly

question_text: Conditional Handover (CHO) is particularly beneficial in NTN because:
options: The network can prepare the target cell in advance and trigger execution automatically when conditions are met, avoiding added signalling latency on a long-RTT link
CHO requires a very short RTT to operate correctly, suiting GEO best
CHO is prohibited in NTN specifications and replaced by fast re-registration
CHO is only applicable when the UE is moving on the ground, not the satellite
correct_answer: The network can prepare the target cell in advance and trigger execution automatically when conditions are met, avoiding added signalling latency on a long-RTT link

question_text: The primary frequency bands targeted by 3GPP NR-NTN specifications for the service link (UE-to-satellite) are:
options: S-band (around 2 GHz) and Ka-band (around 26 GHz)
Only mmWave FR2 bands (24–52 GHz) shared with terrestrial 5G
HF (3–30 MHz) for long-range propagation
The same Ku-band feeder link frequencies used by the gateway
correct_answer: S-band (around 2 GHz) and Ka-band (around 26 GHz)

question_text: Inter-satellite links (ISLs) are most naturally associated with the regenerative payload architecture because:
options: Bent-pipe payloads support ISLs natively without any onboard processing
A regenerative satellite can route and forward data packets, making it practical to relay traffic between satellites toward a distant gateway
ISLs require transparent frequency conversion that only bent-pipe payloads provide
ISLs are prohibited between regenerative satellites under ITU regulations
correct_answer: A regenerative satellite can route and forward data packets, making it practical to relay traffic between satellites toward a distant gateway

question_text: In the RLC layer, the NTN large RTT creates an issue analogous to the TCP window problem, because:
options: The RLC ARQ window may need to be enlarged to allow enough outstanding unacknowledged PDUs so that throughput is not stalled waiting for acknowledgements
RLC ARQ is completely disabled in NTN, removing the window size constraint
RLC window size has no impact on throughput regardless of RTT
The RLC layer is removed from the NTN protocol stack in Release 17
correct_answer: The RLC ARQ window may need to be enlarged to allow enough outstanding unacknowledged PDUs so that throughput is not stalled waiting for acknowledgements

question_text: In LEO NTN, paging areas tend to be larger than in terrestrial networks because:
options: LEO satellites have fewer resources and can only page a small number of UEs
Satellite footprints cover vast geographic areas, and using large paging areas reduces the frequency of tracking area updates as the satellite moves
Large paging areas reduce the total amount of data transmitted to UEs
Paging in NTN follows identical procedures and area sizes as terrestrial 5G
correct_answer: Satellite footprints cover vast geographic areas, and using large paging areas reduces the frequency of tracking area updates as the satellite moves

question_text: Open-loop power control is preferred over closed-loop power control for NTN uplinks because:
options: Closed-loop control is more accurate but requires more UE hardware
The long RTT makes it impractical to rely on fast gNB feedback to adjust UE transmit power in near real-time
Open-loop control uses gNB feedback received within 1 ms
Closed-loop control is mandated by 3GPP for all NTN uplinks
correct_answer: The long RTT makes it impractical to rely on fast gNB feedback to adjust UE transmit power in near real-time

question_text: eMBB (enhanced Mobile BroadBand) services over LEO NTN are achievable, but their throughput is typically lower than terrestrial 5G because of:
options: LEO NTN using a fundamentally different waveform incompatible with eMBB
3GPP prohibiting eMBB services in NTN Release 17
eMBB requiring a latency below 1 ms which is impossible in any NTN
Large free-space path loss and the constrained transmit power of the satellite, limiting link capacity
correct_answer: Large free-space path loss and the constrained transmit power of the satellite, limiting link capacity

question_text: URLLC (Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication) requirements cannot be met by GEO NTN primarily because:
options: GEO satellites are not powerful enough to support URLLC traffic
GEO round-trip delay (~600 ms) far exceeds the sub-millisecond latency target of URLLC
URLLC is defined only for terrestrial networks and excluded from NTN specifications
GEO NTN requires HARQ, which is incompatible with URLLC
correct_answer: GEO round-trip delay (~600 ms) far exceeds the sub-millisecond latency target of URLLC

question_text: Larger subcarrier spacing (higher numerology) in 5G NR is more robust against Doppler-induced inter-carrier interference in NTN because:
options: Larger spacing reduces symbol duration, giving the channel more time to change
A wider subcarrier spacing means the Doppler shift is a smaller fraction of the subcarrier bandwidth, reducing ICI
Lower numerology (smaller subcarrier spacing) is always preferred in NTN
Doppler shift has no relation to subcarrier spacing in OFDM systems
correct_answer: A wider subcarrier spacing means the Doppler shift is a smaller fraction of the subcarrier bandwidth, reducing ICI

question_text: Gateway diversity in NTN means:
options: Multiple geographically separated gateways can serve the same satellite, so if one suffers rain fade the satellite can switch to a clear-sky gateway automatically
Using multiple satellites to serve one ground gateway simultaneously
Providing redundant user terminals at each subscriber site
Using two separate core networks to process gateway traffic
correct_answer: Multiple geographically separated gateways can serve the same satellite, so if one suffers rain fade the satellite can switch to a clear-sky gateway automatically

question_text: Ka-band is attractive for high-throughput satellite (HTS) systems because:
options: Ka-band signals are unaffected by rain, making it ideal in tropical regions
Wide available bandwidths (~500 MHz or more per polarization) enable high throughput, despite more severe rain attenuation and stricter antenna pointing requirements than L- or S-band
Ka-band has narrower bandwidth than L-band, making it more spectrally efficient
Ka-band is exclusively allocated to military satellite communications
correct_answer: Wide available bandwidths (~500 MHz or more per polarization) enable high throughput, despite more severe rain attenuation and stricter antenna pointing requirements than L- or S-band

question_text: NTN is well-suited for massive Machine-Type Communications (mMTC) IoT primarily because:
options: IoT devices require ultra-high bandwidth only satellites can provide
mMTC requires sub-millisecond latency that only LEO satellites can guarantee
IoT devices cannot connect to satellites because they lack GNSS receivers
IoT sensors are often deployed in remote or unpowered locations without terrestrial coverage, and their low data-rate and infrequent transmission requirements suit satellite capacity constraints
correct_answer: IoT sensors are often deployed in remote or unpowered locations without terrestrial coverage, and their low data-rate and infrequent transmission requirements suit satellite capacity constraints

question_text: When a UE moves between satellite beams or between satellites, 5G session continuity mechanisms ensure:
options: PDU sessions are always fully terminated and re-established from scratch
PDU sessions are maintained without application-level disruption, through UPF selection and session anchor management in the 5G core
Session continuity is handled exclusively by the UE without any network involvement
Session continuity is only supported for voice calls, not data sessions
correct_answer: PDU sessions are maintained without application-level disruption, through UPF selection and session anchor management in the 5G core

question_text: A GNSS-capable NTN UE uses its own position and satellite ephemeris to:
options: Authenticate with the satellite's on-board processor
Determine which core network slice to connect to
Request a handover to a terrestrial network when GNSS is available
Pre-compute the uplink frequency offset and timing advance needed to compensate for Doppler shift and propagation delay before transmitting
correct_answer: Pre-compute the uplink frequency offset and timing advance needed to compensate for Doppler shift and propagation delay before transmitting

question_text: Timing pre-compensation in NTN requires the UE to:
options: Delay its uplink transmission to account for the satellite's forward motion
Advance its uplink transmission by an amount equal to the computed propagation delay to the satellite, so the signal arrives within the expected slot window
Ask the gNB to shift the downlink timing by the propagation delay
Transmit at a fixed offset of 0.5 ms regardless of satellite distance
correct_answer: Advance its uplink transmission by an amount equal to the computed propagation delay to the satellite, so the signal arrives within the expected slot window

question_text: Network slicing in 5G NTN allows different service types (broadband, IoT, emergency) to share the same NTN physical resources while maintaining:
options: Independent quality of service, isolation and scheduling policies per slice
A single shared QoS profile for all services to simplify management
Separate physical satellite hardware for each slice
No service differentiation — all slices receive identical treatment
correct_answer: Independent quality of service, isolation and scheduling policies per slice

question_text: 5G NR reference signals (DMRS, CSI-RS, SRS) in NTN must be designed to account for:
options: The large and time-varying delays of the NTN channel, requiring additional reference signal configurations for accurate channel estimation
The complete absence of multipath in the satellite channel
The fact that the NTN channel is perfectly static and needs no estimation
A shorter symbol duration than in terrestrial NR to fit more pilots
correct_answer: The large and time-varying delays of the NTN channel, requiring additional reference signal configurations for accurate channel estimation

question_text: The main factor limiting uplink throughput for direct-to-handset LEO NTN is:
options: The downlink, which is always the bottleneck in NTN systems
Excessive UE transmit power causing interference to neighbouring satellites
The constrained transmit power of handheld UEs (typically 23–26 dBm), which combined with the large path loss sets an upper bound on achievable uplink data rate
The absence of MIMO at the UE, which forces single-antenna transmission
correct_answer: The constrained transmit power of handheld UEs (typically 23–26 dBm), which combined with the large path loss sets an upper bound on achievable uplink data rate

question_text: DVB-S2 (Digital Video Broadcasting — Satellite, Second Generation) is significant for satellite broadband because it:
options: Employs Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM), dynamically selecting the modulation and coding scheme to maximise throughput under varying link conditions
Uses fixed QPSK modulation at a constant code rate regardless of link quality
Is a 3GPP standard designed specifically for 5G NR satellite access
Is a terrestrial broadcast standard not used in satellite systems
correct_answer: Employs Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM), dynamically selecting the modulation and coding scheme to maximise throughput under varying link conditions

question_text: DVB-RCS2 (Return Channel via Satellite, Second Generation) defines:
options: The forward link broadcast from the satellite to all terminals
The interactive return channel from the user terminal to the satellite, enabling two-way broadband satellite services
The ITU standard for GEO orbital slot coordination
The inter-satellite link protocol used in LEO constellations
correct_answer: The interactive return channel from the user terminal to the satellite, enabling two-way broadband satellite services

question_text: A VSAT (Very Small Aperture Terminal) system typically uses:
options: Small dish antennas of 0.6–3.6 m diameter to provide satellite broadband at fixed or mobile sites, usually via GEO satellites in Ku or Ka band
Large parabolic dishes over 10 m in diameter for military communications
LEO satellite constellations exclusively
Phased-array antennas at altitudes above 50 km
correct_answer: Small dish antennas of 0.6–3.6 m diameter to provide satellite broadband at fixed or mobile sites, usually via GEO satellites in Ku or Ka band

question_text: In FDMA (Frequency Division Multiple Access) for satellite systems, a key disadvantage is:
options: Spectrum is wasted when an assigned frequency sub-band is idle because its allocated user has no traffic to send
All users must transmit in the same time slot, causing collisions
FDMA requires the most complex synchronization of all multiple-access schemes
FDMA cannot be used in combination with TDMA on the same satellite
correct_answer: Spectrum is wasted when an assigned frequency sub-band is idle because its allocated user has no traffic to send

question_text: Satellite TDMA (Time Division Multiple Access) requires tight time synchronization across all terminals because:
options: TDMA assigns unique codes to each user and synchronisation prevents code collisions
TDMA uses separate frequencies per terminal and timing prevents frequency drift
Without synchronisation, bursts from different terminals will overlap in time at the satellite, causing interference
Synchronisation is needed only for the ground gateway, not for user terminals
correct_answer: Without synchronisation, bursts from different terminals will overlap in time at the satellite, causing interference

question_text: In CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access), all users share the same bandwidth simultaneously and are separated by unique spreading codes. A critical operational requirement is:
options: That no two users transmit during the same time slot
That each user is assigned a separate frequency channel
That the spreading codes are regenerated every millisecond
Accurate uplink power control, so that no single user's signal overpowers the others (the near-far problem)
correct_answer: Accurate uplink power control, so that no single user's signal overpowers the others (the near-far problem)

question_text: OFDMA (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access) is used in the 5G NR downlink because it:
options: Assigns each user a unique spreading code instead of a frequency sub-band
Is identical to FDMA but with analogue instead of digital carriers
Was designed for single-user access and does not support multi-user scheduling
Allows flexible per-slot scheduling of subcarriers to different users, enabling efficient multi-user resource allocation
correct_answer: Allows flexible per-slot scheduling of subcarriers to different users, enabling efficient multi-user resource allocation

question_text: DFT-spread OFDM (DFT-s-OFDM), also called SC-FDMA, is used in the 5G NR uplink rather than pure OFDMA because it:
options: Has a higher PAPR than OFDM, which suits satellite power amplifiers
Is mandatory for satellite gNBs but prohibited in terrestrial gNBs
Spreads the signal across fewer subcarriers, reducing the transmitted bandwidth
Achieves a lower Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR), which reduces power amplifier stress and is beneficial for power-constrained UE transmitters
correct_answer: Achieves a lower Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR), which reduces power amplifier stress and is beneficial for power-constrained UE transmitters

question_text: The Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) in the 5G SA core is responsible for:
options: Routing user-plane IP packets between the RAN and the internet
Establishing and releasing PDU sessions and managing IP address allocation
UE registration, connection establishment and mobility management including handover decisions
Scheduling radio resource blocks within the gNB
correct_answer: UE registration, connection establishment and mobility management including handover decisions

question_text: The Session Management Function (SMF) in the 5G SA core is responsible for:
options: Handling UE authentication and registration
Performing radio resource scheduling in the gNB
Establishing, modifying and releasing PDU sessions and managing IP address allocation for UEs
Connecting the gNB to the 5G core via the NG interface
correct_answer: Establishing, modifying and releasing PDU sessions and managing IP address allocation for UEs

question_text: The User Plane Function (UPF) in the 5G SA core is the:
options: Control-plane function that manages UE authentication
Data-plane anchor that handles packet routing and forwarding between the RAN and external data networks such as the internet
Radio access node that schedules downlink transmissions
Spectrum management entity that assigns frequencies to operators
correct_answer: Data-plane anchor that handles packet routing and forwarding between the RAN and external data networks such as the internet

question_text: The NG interface in 5G connects the gNB to the 5G core network, with:
options: NG-C (N2) carrying control-plane signalling to the AMF and NG-U (N3) carrying user-plane traffic to the UPF
NG-C carrying user-plane traffic and NG-U carrying control signalling
Both NG-C and NG-U connecting the gNB directly to the internet
The NG interface connecting two neighbouring gNBs to each other
correct_answer: NG-C (N2) carrying control-plane signalling to the AMF and NG-U (N3) carrying user-plane traffic to the UPF

question_text: The Xn interface in 5G connects:
options: The gNB to the 5G core AMF
The UE to the gNB over the air interface
The UPF to external data networks
Neighbouring gNBs to each other, enabling handover coordination, dual connectivity and interference management
correct_answer: Neighbouring gNBs to each other, enabling handover coordination, dual connectivity and interference management

question_text: Phased-array antennas are used in LEO satellite user terminals because they:
options: Are cheaper to manufacture than parabolic dish antennas
Electronically steer narrow beams toward the moving satellite without mechanical movement, enabling rapid tracking at low latency
Do not require any antenna pointing, making them omnidirectional
Can only be used at stationary fixed terminals, not on mobile vehicles
correct_answer: Electronically steer narrow beams toward the moving satellite without mechanical movement, enabling rapid tracking at low latency

question_text: Massive MIMO in 5G NR uses a large number of antenna elements at the gNB to:
options: Reduce the number of antennas compared with 4G LTE
Serve all UEs from a single broad beam to simplify scheduling
Operate only at sub-1 GHz frequencies where wavelengths are large
Form narrow, high-gain beams directed at individual UEs, greatly increasing spectral efficiency through spatial multiplexing
correct_answer: Form narrow, high-gain beams directed at individual UEs, greatly increasing spectral efficiency through spatial multiplexing

question_text: Null-steering in multi-beam satellite antennas suppresses interfering signals by:
options: Placing deep nulls in the antenna radiation pattern in the direction of interferers while maintaining high gain toward intended users
Reducing the satellite's total transmit power across all beams
Assigning orthogonal frequencies to all beams simultaneously
Rotating the satellite's attitude to avoid interfering sources
correct_answer: Placing deep nulls in the antenna radiation pattern in the direction of interferers while maintaining high gain toward intended users

question_text: Higher-order modulation (e.g., 64QAM vs QPSK) transmits more bits per symbol but requires a higher SNR. In satellite systems, higher-order modulation is used when:
options: The link has a large margin above the minimum threshold, typically in good weather or for large dish terminals
The link is close to the minimum SNR threshold and the margin is small
Rain fade has reduced the signal level, necessitating more bits per symbol
Higher-order modulation always operates at a lower SNR than QPSK
correct_answer: The link has a large margin above the minimum threshold, typically in good weather or for large dish terminals

question_text: Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM) in a satellite system monitors the link quality and dynamically selects the MCS to:
options: Fix modulation and coding for the lifetime of a session to avoid overhead
Always select the highest-order modulation regardless of link conditions
Reduce the symbol rate during rain fade, keeping the modulation order constant
Maximise throughput when the link is good and switch to more robust coding during rain fade or shadowing
correct_answer: Maximise throughput when the link is good and switch to more robust coding during rain fade or shadowing

question_text: The carrier-to-noise density ratio C/N₀ at a satellite receiver is determined by combining the transmitter EIRP, free-space path loss, atmospheric losses and the receiver:
options: Transmit power and antenna gain separately
Bit error rate and the required Eb/N₀
Transponder bandwidth and the number of active carriers
Figure of merit G/T (antenna gain divided by system noise temperature)
correct_answer: Figure of merit G/T (antenna gain divided by system noise temperature)

question_text: The satellite power budget must carefully balance onboard power generation against consumption because:
options: Satellites use nuclear reactors with unlimited power but limited cooling
HPAs consume negligible power compared with the onboard processor
Solar panel area is constrained by mass and structural limits, and the high-power amplifiers (HPAs) are the dominant power consumers on the payload
Solar panel technology is mature enough that power is never a constraint
correct_answer: Solar panel area is constrained by mass and structural limits, and the high-power amplifiers (HPAs) are the dominant power consumers on the payload

question_text: In a hub-and-spoke satellite network, remote VSAT terminals communicate via the satellite to a central hub, which:
options: Is located in orbit on the satellite itself
Connects the satellite network to the terrestrial internet or PSTN and provides high-power, high-bandwidth uplinking to the satellite
Is replaced by a full-mesh ISL topology in all modern systems
Requires no uplink because it only receives traffic from the satellite
correct_answer: Connects the satellite network to the terrestrial internet or PSTN and provides high-power, high-bandwidth uplinking to the satellite

question_text: A full-mesh satellite network enabled by ISLs or multi-spot beams allows:
options: All communication to be routed through a single hub regardless of ISLs
Terminals to bypass the satellite and communicate directly by radio
Terminals to communicate directly with each other through the satellite without routing through a terrestrial hub, reducing latency for terminal-to-terminal traffic
A full-mesh to be established only with GEO satellites, not LEO
correct_answer: Terminals to communicate directly with each other through the satellite without routing through a terrestrial hub, reducing latency for terminal-to-terminal traffic

question_text: A satellite link availability specification of 99.9% per year means the link is unavailable for approximately:
options: About 1 second per year, requiring a negligible link margin
About 8.8 hours per year, so the link margin must be sized to withstand rain fades for all but that time
About 36.5 days per year, requiring a very large link margin
Availability specifications do not affect the required link margin
correct_answer: About 8.8 hours per year, so the link margin must be sized to withstand rain fades for all but that time

question_text: Most satellite systems use Frequency Division Duplex (FDD) rather than Time Division Duplex (TDD) because:
options: The uplink and downlink already use different frequency bands (e.g., 14 GHz up / 11 GHz down in Ku band), naturally accommodating simultaneous two-way transmission
TDD requires two satellite transponders while FDD needs only one
TDD is prohibited by ITU regulations for satellite systems
FDD has lower hardware complexity in the satellite transponder than TDD
correct_answer: The uplink and downlink already use different frequency bands (e.g., 14 GHz up / 11 GHz down in Ku band), naturally accommodating simultaneous two-way transmission

question_text: In 5G NR, PDSCH scheduling is performed by the gNB using:
options: A fixed static resource assignment programmed at network deployment and never changed
Uplink control signalling sent by the UE to reserve its own resources
Random access preambles on the PRACH that initiate scheduling
DCI (Downlink Control Information) transmitted on the PDCCH, which tells the UE which resource blocks carry its data in each slot
correct_answer: DCI (Downlink Control Information) transmitted on the PDCCH, which tells the UE which resource blocks carry its data in each slot
